name: targets-selected
description: Covers this integration's runZero half -- the target-selection stage -- and stops deliberately at the GMP boundary: the stop is made deterministic rather than left to a connection timeout by using transport=ssh with neither ssh_password nor ssh_private_key set, which gmp_connect rejects up front, so the run ends on a guard and never opens a socket. (The GMP leg itself is exercised by the scan-started, task-rejected, and hangup-rollback scenarios beside this one, over the harness's GMP TLS responder.) Everything before that boundary is real and asserted. The CSV body is the genuine /api/v1.0/export/org/assets.csv output -- all 57 columns in the order runzero/csvwriter/asset.go writes them, CRLF line endings, and a leading UTF-8 BOM, which the writer really does emit and which makes the first header literally '\ufeffid'. That the walk still finds its column proves the reader tolerates it. `address` is GetFirstAddress(), ONE primary address per row, while `addresses_scope` beside it is every address space-joined; four of the five rows are deliberately multi-homed so those columns differ, and reading the wrong one selects nothing at all rather than coincidentally the same count. The five rows exercise the whole selection: two rows share 10.42.0.11 and must dedupe to one target; an IPv6 row is written fully expanded and must be selected in its canonical short form, since the script keys on str(ip_address(addr)) rather than on the raw text; and the last row is a hostname-only asset whose `address` is empty, which is ordinary for anything discovered without a network observation and must be skipped rather than sent to Greenbone as an empty target. '3 target address(es) selected' is therefore the assertion that all three of those happened -- 4 would mean the duplicate survived, 5 would mean the empty address did.
